paras: The Charleston riot of May 1919 was an attack on Black residents of Charleston, South Carolina, by sailors from the city's navy yard and training camp, joined by some white civilians, on the night of May 10, 1919. Two Black men, James Talbot and Isaac Doctor, were reported killed, and thirteen to seventeen Black people and several sailors were wounded. Black newspapers likened it to the 1917 Houston riot and stressed that only Black people were attacked.
Accounts of the first clash differ, but most place it about nine o'clock on Saturday night in or near a poolroom around Market, King and Beaufain streets.

Bluejackets, "assisted by some civilians, apparently," then attacked Black people in the streets, and the police could not stop them. The rioters broke up a restaurant for clubs, took rifles from two shooting galleries, and wrecked a Black-owned barber shop on King street until an army and a naval officer drove them off. They stopped trolley cars, removed every passenger who was not white, and shot several as they were pulled from the cars. The Continental Press dispatch counted over 1,000 bluejackets and over 300 white civilians, and said policemen were stripped of their clubs and pistols.

Rear Admiral Benjamin C. Bryan, commandant of the navy yard, sent marines into town and had the sailors trucked back to base. According to the Afro-American, marines then searched every Black man on the streets, and shots were fired at the police station from an automobile carrying Black men, hitting no one. The Afro-American listed Talbot and Doctor as dead, named thirteen Black wounded, and reported five white men hurt; a later police count gave two Black men killed, seventeen injured, and seven bluejackets wounded.

Police and military authorities made more than a score of arrests, and two sailors, named as Cohen and Holtay, were charged with killing Doctor and held for an inquest before Coroner Mansfield. No report of the inquest's finding or of a trial appears in the coverage. Mayor Hyde promised an investigation and said "All loss of property will be restored by the city," while the Continental Press complained that the sailors were known but unprosecuted.

The Baltimore Afro-American's front page of May 16 read "Sailor Taunts Negro" and "Business Place Of Colored People Sho[t] Up," over lists of the dead and wounded. The Chicago Defender's "Sailors Stage Bloody Battles in Streets of Charleston" called the Houston rioters "more orderly" than sailors who killed people going home from work. The Cleveland Advocate headlined "Eight Killed in Race Riot," though its text reported six men wounded, and closed that the bluejackets "were after Colored people only."

The Savannah Tribune set the Charleston blue-jackets beside recent lynchings in an editorial on Southern lawlessness, and Cayton's Weekly noted both sides were led by men back from overseas. Later items were brief: the Defender's own investigation on May 24 and the police count in the Cleveland Gazette and the Wisconsin Weekly Blade.

The Afro-American's headline said a taunted Black man threw a brick at a sailor, while its text said he bit the sailor. The Advocate said a Black man was accused of shooting a bluejacket who insulted him, and the Gazette named Isaac Doctor as the shooter. The Continental Press said a drunk sailor drew a revolver in a poolroom and was shot in the scuffle, while the Defender's investigator traced the riot to $8 sailors gave a Black man for whiskey he never delivered.
The Defender's wire also reported two sailors and four citizens dead, but the named dead and the police count agree on two Black men killed.

reader.title: Charleston riot of May 1919
bases: Hundreds or thousands of sailors, joined by some white civilians, attacked Black people across downtown Charleston, pulling them from streetcars and wrecking Black-owned businesses, with witnesses agreeing only Black people were targeted (A4, A6, A7, A2).

Separate Charleston dispatches in the Baltimore Afro-American, Chicago Defender (Continental Press) and Cleveland Advocate, and a police count carried by the Cleveland Gazette and Wisconsin Weekly Blade, agree on a sailors' riot against Black residents on the night of May 10 with Black dead (A2, A4, A6, A12, A13).

accounts.label: Baltimore Afro-American Charleston dispatch
accounts.gist: Trouble began about nine o'clock at Market and Charles streets when a Black man bit a sailor after taunts (headline: replied with a brick); mob rule followed, two Black men dead, thirteen wounded, five white men hurt.

accounts.label: Cleveland Advocate Charleston dispatch
accounts.gist: A Black man was accused of shooting a bluejacket in a poolroom after an insult; bluejackets, with some civilians, attacked Black people only.

accounts.label: Continental Press (Chicago Defender)
accounts.gist: A drunk sailor abused a King street poolroom owner, drew a revolver and was shot in a scuffle; over 1,000 sailors and 300 white civilians then rioted, and two sailors and four citizens died.

accounts.label: Defender investigator
accounts.gist: The riot grew from a Black man's failure to return with whiskey for which sailors had advanced $8; five sailors with bricks came looking for him and a pool-room fight followed.

accounts.label: Police count (wire)
accounts.gist: Two Black men killed, seventeen injured, seven bluejackets wounded; the Gazette version adds that the sailors acted after Isaac Doctor shot one of them.

framing.detail: Afro-American front page: 'Sailor Taunts Negro', 'Business Place Of Colored People Sho[t] Up', with lists of the dead and wounded and an account of men 'knocked down without cause'.
Defender: 'Sailors Stage Bloody Battles in Streets of Charleston', likening it to Houston 1917 and saying the sailors killed innocent people and went unprosecuted.
Cleveland Advocate: 'Eight Killed in Race Riot', closing that all witnesses agreed the bluejackets were after Black people only.
Savannah Tribune editorial set the Charleston blue-jackets beside Southern lynchings as proof of lawlessness.
Cleveland Gazette and Wisconsin Weekly Blade ran the police count as brief news items, the Gazette with the version that Doctor shot a sailor.

record_check.record: A sailor taunted a Negro and was hit with a brick, starting a race riot
record_check.dossier: The brick appears only in the Afro-American headline; its text says the Black man bit the sailor, and other papers give a poolroom shooting, a drunk sailor's revolver, or a whiskey-money dispute.
Sailors ('bluejackets') from the Charleston navy yard and naval training camp, joined by some white civilians.
13 in the Afro-American list; 17 in the later police count.
Five white men (Afro-American) or seven bluejackets (police count).
The Defender's wire reported two sailors dead; no other paper did.

record_check.record: a colored man attacked a sailor with a bite following taunting words
record_check.dossier: One of six versions of the trigger; the mob's attack on Black residents generally carried no accusation against the victims.

info: Saturday night, May 10, 1919, into Sunday morning, May 11
Downtown Charleston: Market, King, Beaufain and George streets, Marion Square; begun at or near a poolroom
Dead: James Talbot and Isaac Doctor; thirteen wounded named, including Moses Gadsen, Peter Irvin, Andrew Witchell, Edward Campbell, Thomas Ingram, Gus Cannon, Clifford Singleton, James Wilson

Versions differ on the trigger: a Black man bit a sailor after taunts; a Black man threw a brick at a taunting sailor; a Black man accused of shooting a bluejacket who had insulted him; a drunk sailor who drew a revolver in a poolroom was shot; a Black man failed to return with whiskey bought with $8 of sailors' money; Isaac Doctor shot a sailor
Sailors ('bluejackets') from the Charleston navy yard and naval training camp, joined by some white civilians
2 (James Talbot, Isaac Doctor); the Defender's wire said four citizens dead
Defender's May 16 dispatch said nothing had been done to prosecute the sailors; no inquest verdict or trial reported

sources.note: Front-page headline deck ('Marines Called', 'Sailor Taunts Negro, Who Replies With A Brick', business places shot up) and 'The Dead: James Talbot, Isaac Doctor'; rest of column is other news.
Charleston May 10 dispatch: two colored men dead, thirteen wounded (named), five white men hurt; marines searched every colored man; barber shops shot up; bayonet incidents under martial law.
quotes: Marines were sent for and searched every colored man on the streets.
Numbers of men were knocked down without cause and left to be removed by friends.

sources.note: Continuation: start at Market and Charles streets (bite after taunting words); restaurant, shooting galleries, barber shop; sailors Cohen and Holtay charged with killing Doctor, inquest set; station house fired on; more than a score of arrests.
quotes: when a colorado man attacked a sailor with a bite following taunting words
Cohen and Holtay the two saints charged with killing Doctors have been turned over to the authorities

sources.note: Continental Press, Charleston May 16: compares riot to Houston 1917; over 1,000 bluejackets; two sailors and four citizens dead; police disarmed; non-white trolley passengers removed and shot.
quotes: A plot similar to the one in Houston, Tex., in August, 1917, was staged in this city last Saturday by sailors from the Charleston navy yard.
Trolley cars were stopped and all passengers who were not white were removed.

sources.note: Continuation of A4: over 300 white civilians joined; drunk sailor drew revolver in King street poolroom and was shot; sailors known but not prosecuted; War Department and Washington to be asked to act.
quotes: Although the sailors who took part in the riot are known, nothing has been done to prosecute them.

sources.note: Headline 'Eight Killed'; Charleston May 10 dispatch: colored man accused of shooting a bluejacket in a poolroom; bluejackets with some civilians attacked colored people; Adm. Bryan; shooting galleries; barber shop; trolley incident.
quotes: bluejackets, assisted by some civilians, apparently, attacked many Colored people

sources.note: Continuation of A6 (embedded in another column): Black men taken from streetcars and shot; several thousand bluejackets; 'bluejackets were after Colored people only'.
quotes: All witnesses agree that the bluejackets were after Colored people only, as no white civilians were molested.

sources.note: Editorial on Southern lawlessness and lynching citing the Charleston blue-jackets: 'Negroes only were the object of attack.'
quotes: Or (as in the case of the Charleston blue-jackets) "Negroes only were the object of attack."

sources.note: Editorial paragraph: race riot in Charleston last Saturday, both sides led by soldiers and sailors returned from overseas.
quotes: both sides were led by black and white soldiers and sailors recently returned from overseas

sources.note: Defender representative's investigation: dispute over $8 advanced for whiskey; five bluejackets with bricks at King and George streets; pool-room fight; Mayor Hyde promises investigation and restoration of property loss (OCR garbled).
quotes: All loss of property will be restored by the city.

sources.note: Charleston social notes wish recovery to those injured in 'the race riot on Saturday, May 16' (date differs).
News brief: riot Saturday night May 10, two Afro-Americans killed, seventeen wounded, seven bluejackets wounded; some 2,000 sailors after one was shot by Isaac Doctor.
quotes: some 2,000 of the latter taking part in the shooting of one of their number by Isaac Doctor, an Afro-American

sources.note: Late wire brief: police count two Negroes ('nuggets' in OCR) killed, seventeen injured, seven bluejackets wounded.
quotes: A count by the police today showed two nuggets were killed and seventeen injured in a riot last night with civilians and sailors.
